qa.question: Should units 11 and 12 stay operating when EIA still shows testing?
qa.finding: OG&E said in September 2026 that unit 11 passed its tests and would enter service in October. The October 28, 2026 earnings call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ describes both units as added capacity. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx still shows both as construction complete, not yet in commercial operation, planned October 2026.
qa.recommendation: Leave both units as operating. Check the OG&E ribbon cutting release in November 2026 for the exact date.
qa.note: I did not find a document that gives the commercial operation date. Sierra Club data also shows construction, but it is not cited.

qa.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to units 13 and 14?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 13 and 14, each 224 MW, planned February 2029. The earnings call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ gives 440 MW for both, which is 220 MW each.
qa.recommendation: Treat EIA generator 13 as unit 13 and generator 14 as unit 14. Both are 224 MW in EIA and in GEM, so no capacity change.
qa.note: OG&E's own figure of 440 MW total is a rounded plant total.

qa.question: How do SPP queue dates ERAS-2025-010 and GEN-2024-GR1 fit units 13 and 14?
qa.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists ERAS-2025-010, a 496 MW combustion turbine at the Horseshoe Lake substation with an in-service date of April 2028, and GEN-2024-GR1, 492 MW. OG&E and EIA say units 13 and 14 start in 2029.
qa.recommendation: Leave the start year at 2029. The queue entries are about 496 MW, close to two 224 MW units plus margin.
qa.note: I did not open the 2025 commission docket orders to check for an earlier date, because the call summary and EIA both say 2029 or later.

qa.question: Is unit 15 a 2031 start, or is queue entry ERAS-2025-004 for 2029 the same project?
qa.finding: The October 28, 2026 call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ says unit 15 is 755 MW and enters service in 2031. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists ERAS-2025-004, a 756.2 MW combined cycle at the same substation dated April 2029.
qa.recommendation: Keep 2031 from the owner's statement and treat the queue entry as the same project with an earlier placeholder date.
qa.note: The queue is a lead only.

qa.question: Is the Energy and Policy Institute proposed record for Horseshoe Lake wrong for unit 10?
qa.finding: The Energy and Policy Institute Oil and Gas Watch record at https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/rec_d4f1u5oq7easr8ra1f60 lists the plant as proposed. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists unit 10 as operating, 60.5 MW, started 2001.
qa.recommendation: Leave unit 10 as operating. The proposed label most likely reflects the new units 13 to 15.
qa.note: The record page is drawn by script and its text could not be read by the page checker.

qa.question: Is there a document that states Backup Power for the Horseshoe Lake units?
qa.finding: I found no document that says whether any Horseshoe Lake unit is a backup power unit. All sources describe the units as grid supply for OG&E customers.
qa.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no on all ten units and leave the source box empty.
qa.note: Searched the 2026 OG&E plan, the September 2026 news release and EIA-860M. None uses the term.

qa.question: Where do units 6 and ST7 stand in GEM, and what is their source?
qa.finding: Both are retired in GEM with 2024 retirement years. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists unit 6 retired January 2024 and ST7 retired December 2024.
qa.recommendation: Leave both as retired, and use the EIA-860M table as the source of the retirement year.
qa.note: The September 2024 notes in the status detail say to be retired and were not changed.
